analyst_view.overall: Early view: Andorra are 18th and still have their postponed home game with Mallorca to play; how the squad, and goalkeeper Jesús Owono in particular, recover from the death of Tenerife's Jesús de Miguel is hard to judge from here. Oviedo are ninth and have a good away record (four wins in seven) under Julián Calero. The bans in the brief for Owono, De León and Akman should be served at Almería on 14 November.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. I lean higher: Andorra's home games have averaged three and a half goals and Oviedo's away games over three, with both defences conceding regularly.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.0 corners. Andorra keep the ball (74% possession at Tenerife) but did not turn it into many corners, and I found nothing else to move the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.9 cards. I lean higher: Andorra are among the most-booked teams in the division (40 yellows and two reds in 12 games), and Oviedo took five yellows at Cádiz, with Carlos D. already on five.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots. I lean lower: Andorra took only 11 shots at Tenerife despite dominating the ball, and Oviedo had 12 at Cádiz.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target. With open games on both sides but modest shot volume, I stay near the site's number.
